hints.content:
To find the average rate of change $(ARC)$ of the function $h$ over the interval $[2,6]$, we need to take the total change in the function value over the interval (which is the difference of its values at the endpoints) and divide it by the length of the interval:

 $ARC_{[2,6]}= \dfrac{h(6)-h(2)}{6-2}$.

Note that this is the same as finding the slope of the line connecting the points on the graph that correspond to the endpoints of the interval:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The graph is a group of line segments that contains the following points: the point negative six, nine, the point negative four, four, the point zero, zero, the point two, two, the point five, four, and the point six, nine. The point two, two and the point six, nine are connected by a solid line segment. There is a dashed segment from two, two to six, two. There is another dashed segment from six, two to six, nine.

hints.content:
According to the graph, $h(\blue{2})=\pink{2}$ and $h(\blue{6})=\pink{9}$. Therefore, the average rate of change we are looking for is:

$\dfrac{\pink{9}-\pink{2}}{\blue{6}-\blue{2}}=\dfrac{7}{4}$.
